To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
creativity is a silent and elusive quality that is not readily measured, yet it is a quality that is essential to the teaching of design and problem solving.
1) creativity can be stimulated through design and problem solving; 2) design and problem solving activities are not always creative, and 3) creativity can be enhanced in technology education.
the creative process is an important goal of the technology education curriculum.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a conceptual framework for the teaching of creative problem-solving in technology education, and the development of a curriculum that will support the framework.
the nature of creativity and the development of creative thinking.
the nature and development of design and problem-solving abilities.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
creativity is a complex and elusive phenomenon that can be stimulated by a variety of instructional approaches.
creativity is not a unitary construct, but rather a set of dispositions and abilities that can be cultivated in children by a range of instructional strategies and activities.
creativity is a complex phenomenon that can be stimulated and enhanced through design teaching, and that design teaching is one means of developing creative abilities in children.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
creativity is a process which involves the use of divergent thinking, convergent thinking, and the ability to communicate ideas in the form of artifacts.
the creative process is a silent process, which is not readily amenable to the usual methods of curriculum, instruction or assessment.
we have developed a framework that can be used to help students develop creative solutions to technology problems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
creativity is not an isolated or singular attribute of individuals, and that it cannot be taught or learned by itself.

creativity in technology education is a complex, multi-dimensional, and elusive construct that is difficult to define and measure, and that the development of creative dispositions and performance is an elusive and long term goal.

creativity can be taught, and that the teaching of creativity can be made more effective through the development of a conceptual framework that is both grounded in the literature on creativity, and that is sensitive to the needs of technology education.
